chapters.headline: Scoot's 27 or Jrue's +33: who actually won this game in Milwaukee?
Dame's 33 in Milwaukee and a win that was closer than 1-15 says
Camara's third quarter: four threes, three blocked threes
The bench and center minutes: Clingan, Yang, Carlson

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Jack. You sound tired.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: I am tired. I ate dinner at nine-thirty last night, standing at the counter. Bran flakes, straight out of the box. Somewhere in the fourth quarter I forgot dinner was a thing people do.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Bran flakes at the counter. You eat like a man waiting on a jury.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: That's how the fourth quarter felt. How was the bar?

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Loud, for a Thursday. The bartender had the over, so he wanted points, anybody's points. Every time we coughed it up and Milwaukee ran out for a layup, he slapped the bar like he'd scored it himself. Best night of his life.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: So he's the only guy in Portland who enjoyed that stretch.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Him, and me for the whole second quarter. Which is my case. Scoot's my player of the night.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Of course he is. I've got Jrue.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Hear me out first. Jrue was great, twenty-two, seven assists, four steals, nobody's arguing. But Jrue doing Jrue things is why we got him. That's the sticker on the box. Scoot going eight for twelve, five for six from three, after the month he's had? Nobody had that coming. And the moment that got me was the end of the first. Jrue's got a clean look above the break. He swings it to Scoot in the left corner instead, and Scoot buries it at the buzzer.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: I loved that play. I rewound it.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: That's a vet telling a kid, I trust your shot over mine. Then Scoot goes out and owns the second quarter, and Nori just leaves him out there. Ten-plus minutes. Doesn't touch it. A coach trusting a kid. That's my whole thing.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Okay. Let me play the other side for a second. You skipped your own best evidence. Late in the fourth it's a game, and Portland has to take it back. What happens on the next trip down?

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Jrue hits a three.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Ties it. That's the moment a game against a one-and-fifteen team turns into the loss everybody screenshots, and he shuts the door. Then the steal on Herro and the layup. Which, side note, I still can't get used to Herro in a Bucks jersey. Anyway. Where was Scoot in the fourth?

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Quiet. I know. I'll give you that.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Jrue's plus thirty-three in thirty-one minutes. Scoot's plus seventeen. I know that number lies plenty. But a gap that wide on a night like this tells you who was holding it together. Scoot built the cushion. Jrue kept anybody from spending it.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: But you just said it. Scoot built the cushion. No second quarter, no lead for Jrue to guard. And Jrue's prettiest play all night was handing Scoot that corner three. So the best thing Jrue did was make Scoot's night happen, and you want to give Jrue the trophy for it? Come on.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Ha. That's a lawyer's argument.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: It's a good lawyer's argument.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: It's decent. So tell me about those five threes. How many were him catching it off somebody else's work, and how many did he make off his own dribble? If it's mostly the first kind, I'd guess good passing found him and the jumper hasn't changed much. And it's a tired team on the second night of a back-to-back, twelve straight losses. I'd call it a really good Thursday and wait.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: I honestly don't know the split. A lot of them felt like rhythm shots, the ball moving to him. So, fair. And okay, that's the optimism talking, because I already think he's arriving. What I saw was a guy who quit looking for the escape pass. Seven trips to the line, six makes. He was going at people. Shooters get their confidence back one make at a time, and he got about eleven of them in one night.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: I liked that he went quiet in the fourth, too. Kid has a hot night and lets the older guy close? Plenty of guys jack up four bad ones trying to make it a forty-point story. He didn't.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: See, now you're on my side.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: I'm splitting it. Scoot gets the story, Jrue gets the win. And I'm a little suspicious of my own one-game reflex. I've talked myself out of young guys before and been very wrong about it.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Write that down. So what are you watching Saturday?

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Shot choice. Say his first two threes miss at the Garden. Does he keep shooting, or go back to attacking and getting to the line? If he's still at the line on a cold night, I'll start believing.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Mine's his face. First two miss, does he keep going downhill, or start glancing at the bench? And someday soon I want him closing one of these himself instead of watching Jrue do it.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: How's your dad on Jrue? There were three ugly turnovers in there he'd have hated.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Ha. He called. Eleven seconds. 'Jrue. Old man.' Click.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Compliment or complaint?

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: I think both. And I think it was about himself a little too. I didn't ask. I'll find out Sunday.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Speaking of old men. Dame drops thirty-three in the building that let him go. Milwaukee waived him, and he went out there and did that. It landed on me more than I expected.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Landed how?

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Some weeks the phone doesn't ring. Two years ago a reorg decided how my last job ended. I'd like to pick the next ending myself. That's all. It's a point guard on a hot night and I'm getting sentimental about my calendar.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Hey. You're allowed. And for what it's worth, you sound like a guy who's still picking. I came home from Tokyo half-convinced I was retreating, and some nights I still think that. Dame went back to the place that knew him first and he's scoring thirty. Going home and quitting are two different moves.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Huh. Yeah. Okay, I'll take that. Thank you.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Now the part I can't let go. We gave it away twenty times. Thirty-one points off those. And a bunch turned into layups before we were even back on defense. That's how you let a one-and-fifteen team hang around.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: I'll push on that. Milwaukee threw it away seventeen times and gave up twenty-eight off them. Two tired, short-handed teams flinging it around. Deni's out, Ja's out, everybody's playing a job that isn't theirs. My hunch is it's mostly noise.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: I don't buy that. We shot fifty-three percent, forty from three. Shoot like that and the worst team in the league should be gone by the third. Instead we let them hang around. Habits follow you to New York. I'm happy with the win. I'm just not hanging it on the wall.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Then answer this. If the problem is nobody steadying things with Ja and Deni gone, why does Dame finish with zero assists and four turnovers?

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Ugh. I've got nothing on that one. He was hunting his own shot and it mostly worked. He said himself he's not all the way back yet, so I'm hoping the passing is the last thing to come.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: And the side plot I'd follow all year: Portland controls some of Milwaukee's future picks. Every Bucks loss makes those look a little better.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Which feels gross to root for, and I'm going to root for it anyway.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Camara. Scoreless at the half, and then that third quarter. I watched it twice and I still can't tell you what flipped. You?

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: I've got a theory. Early on he looks like he's thinking about every shot. Then he chases Herro down and blocks his three from behind. Then he hits a three. Then another. Blocks Burries. More threes. Blocks Jakucionis. Stop, shoot, stop, shoot. I think the defense fed the offense. He quit thinking and started hunting.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Okay, but here's my question. Does that hold up? Simpler version: Milwaukee kept leaving him, and a few finally dropped. That's a heater. Nobody plans around a heater.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: The threes, sure, those come and go. But nobody blocks a three from behind by accident. You chase, you read the release, you decide the guy isn't getting it off. He can make that choice every night. A guy who hits his threes some nights and erases shooters every night is a starter on a good team.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: That part I'll give you. Three blocks, two steals, four assists. That's why he's out there thirty-seven minutes. The threes are a bonus.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: And then he's minus two. In a ten-point win. After all that.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Which is the film I'd actually want. Somebody else on the floor was giving it back while he was cooking. Who?

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: My guess is the two-big stretches. Which, conveniently, is where I wanted to go anyway.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Clingan, thirteen boards in twenty-six minutes, plus three. Two of five, not pretty, but the glass was ours when he was out there. Then he sits in the fourth, and Yang comes in with the game still live.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: And I've got skin in this. Couple days ago I said if Yang isn't in the rotation by the new year, he goes to the G League, and you said you'd hold me to it.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: I did. And look at last night. Sidy finds him, floater, we're back in front in the fourth. Then he drops it off to Jrue for the and-one, a beat before the defense knew. A kid who hasn't played real fourth quarters, taking a shot he trusts.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: That's a point for you. Nori doesn't put a guy out there in a close fourth if he's given up on him. He's finding out. But hold on. Carlson plays ten minutes, scores nothing, team's plus five. Yang has two points, two turnovers, oh for two at the line, minus two. You'd credit Carlson's good minutes to his teammates and Yang's bad ones to his future. Same standard?

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Ha. No. Different standard, and I know it. Yang gave me plays I can point at, the floater and the pass to Jrue. Carlson gave me nothing to point at, good or bad. And the Yang-Carlson pairing in the second was rough, I'll own that. Yang at the four, chasing guards through screens, is nobody's plan. He moved back to the five in the third and looked like a different guy.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Two plays in twelve minutes is thin.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: It's thin. The turnovers are real. But I'd rather he cough it up in a fourth that matters than in garbage time. Garbage time teaches him nothing.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Then let's pin the bet down so neither of us weasels. What counts as in the rotation?

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Plays most nights. Real minutes, at the five. And at least one more game where he's out there with it close. Deal?

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Deal. And Tonje, oh for three in six minutes, all threes. Short leash.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: He was pressing. Six minutes, three threes, trying to make the whole night count. I just want him to get another one before anybody makes up their mind.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Which brings us to my building. Knicks beat Minnesota one-oh-two to ninety-nine, and it came down to a whistle in the last seconds that Minnesota is going to be mad about for a week. So I'm not discussing it.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: You'll discuss it by Saturday. And Towns going up against the team that traded him? A little spite. I love it.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Memphis is ten and four, and that's a rebuild that forgot to be bad.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: And Wemby had some shot against the Clippers that I'm told is half shot, half dunk. Spurs bounce right back after Detroit. They're coming to our place after this road trip, so enjoy it now.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: Okay, Saturday. If Deni's back, I think you're dangerous. If you're still short and still throwing it around, the Garden eats that alive. I'd like to be calm about it. I won't be.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: Good. Twenty turnovers at the Garden and I'll hear you yelling from Portland.

transcript.speaker: jack
transcript.text: And I'll eat a real dinner first. Something with a plate. See you, Mikey.

transcript.speaker: mikey
transcript.text: See you, Jack. Say hi to the cheap seats.
